clinical.citation: A unique de novo gain-of-function variant in CAMK4 associated with intellectual disability and hyperkinetic movement disorder (PMID: 30262571)

variants.description: c.981+1G>A (essential splice-site; 77-nt out-of-frame deletion in the transcript, p.Lys303Serfs*28)
phenotypes: milestone delay
intellectual disability
autism
ataxia
mixed hyperkinetic movement disorder
severe generalized dystonia

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo on trio exome sequencing. The variant is absent from variant catalogs, and variants depleting the regulatory domain are unobserved in the population. cDNA analysis showed a stable transcript with a premature stop codon in the last exon, losing the C-terminal regulatory domain. Proband-derived cells showed increased CaMKIV activity, consistent with gain of function.

biological.citation: Lung cancer stem cell study - TIPRL Regulates Stemness and Survival in Lung Cancer Stem Cells through CaMKK2-CaMK4-CREB Feedback Loop Activation (PMID: 39076120)
biological.summary: In lung cancer stem cells, TIPRL binds CaMKK2 and sustains CaMKK2-mediated activation of CaMK4. CaMK4 phosphorylates CREB at Ser129/Ser133, driving expression of Bcl2 and HMG20A. CREB in turn activates TIPRL transcription, forming a positive feedback loop that supports stemness, survival and drug resistance.

biological.citation: Camk4-/- imiquimod psoriasis study - Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IV promotes imiquimod-induced psoriatic inflammation via macrophages and keratinocytes in mice (PMID: 35869084)
biological.summary: CaMK4 expression is increased in psoriatic human skin and in IMQ-treated mouse skin. Camk4-/- mice and macrophage-specific Camk4 deletion show reduced psoriasis severity. CaMK4 suppresses macrophage IL-10 production and, in keratinocytes, inhibits apoptosis and promotes proliferation and S100A8/CAMP expression.

biological.citation: CaMK4 in acute lung injury - CaMK4 Promotes Acute Lung Injury Through NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation in Type II Alveolar Epithelial Cell (PMID: 35734175)
biological.summary: CaMK4 phosphorylation is increased in the lungs of LPS-induced ALI mice. In A549 AEC II cells, KN-93 or CaMK4 siRNA reduced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, caspase-1 p20 and IL-1β/IL-18 production. KN-93 ameliorated lung injury in mice.

biological.citation: CaMK4 downstream of α1G T-type channel - CaMK4 is a downstream effector of the α(1G) T-type calcium channel to determine the angiogenic potential of pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (PMID: 34586897)
biological.summary: CaMK4 is expressed in pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells. Blocking or knocking down the α1G channel reduced CaMK4 phosphorylation but not CaMK2 phosphorylation. CaMK4 inhibition or knockdown reduced proliferation, migration and network formation without altering Akt phosphorylation, so α1G-Ca2+-CaMK4 acts independently of the Akt pathway.

biological.citation: RNAi screen of host kinases - RNA Interference Screening Reveals Host CaMK4 as a Regulator of Cryptococcal Uptake and Pathogenesis (PMID: 28970273)
biological.summary: An siRNA screen of 868 kinases and phosphatases identified CaMK4 as a specific regulator of C. neoformans uptake by host cells. Pharmacological inhibition of CaMK4 reproduced the phagocytosis defect. CaMK4-deficient mice survived longer after infection, with reduced pattern recognition receptor expression on phagocytes.

biological.citation: Uygur hypertension association - CAMK4 gene variation is associated with hypertension in a Uygur population (PMID: 26909912)
biological.summary: The CAMK4 variant rs10491334 was associated with hypertension in the Uygur group: T-allele frequency was 12.5% in cases vs 6.38% in controls. No association was found in the Han or Kazak groups.
biological.sample_size: 1224 hypertensive patients and 967 controls (Han, Kazak, Uygur)

biological.summary: CAMK4 acts downstream of CAMKK2 and overlaps with it in expression in mouse brain. In Camk4-/- mice, loss of CAMK4 caused abnormal post-translational modification and turnover of transferrin in cerebellum and liver, with iron dyshomeostasis. In CRISPR-edited HEK293 clones, CAMKK2-CAMK4 deficiency altered intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis and transferrin/TFRC complex interactions.

biological.citation: CaMK4 in atherosclerosis - Impaired CAMK4 Activity Limits Atherosclerosis and Reprograms Myelopoiesis (PMID: 40336480)
biological.summary: CaMK4 expression is increased in advanced/unstable human carotid plaque and in plaque macrophages. Camk4-/- mice developed smaller, more stable lesions, with monocytosis skewed to Ly6c-low monocytes and more myeloid progenitors. Higher Nr4a1 and ATF6-dependent transcription were seen, and CaMK4 silencing in human monocytes recapitulated the phenotype.

CaMK4 is upregulated in the uteroplacental complex and spleen in LPS-induced abortion in mice. The inhibitor KN-93 reduced Th17 infiltration and function and reversed fetal resorption. CaMK4 acts through the AKT/mTOR pathway to promote Th17 expansion.
Anti-PLA2R antibody stimulation of human podocytes increased calcium levels and CaMK4 expression, alongside apoptosis and cytoskeletal damage.
